name: MAX11614EEE+
title: Low-power 4-, 8- and 12-channel 12-bit I2C ADCs
summary: MAX11612 to MAX11617 are 12-bit successive-approximation ADCs with 4, 8 or 12 inputs, an internal reference, clock and track/hold, read over an I2C-compatible bus at 400 kHz or 1.7 MHz. The MAX11614 has 8 single-ended or 4 differential inputs, runs from 4.5 V to 5.5 V and has a 4.096 V internal reference; the odd-numbered parts run from 2.7 V to 3.6 V with 2.048 V. Throughput reaches 94.4 ksps at 670 µA, and automatic shutdown between conversions brings the current under 1 µA at low rates.

notes: MAX11612/MAX11613 force CS3 and CS2 to 0; MAX11614/MAX11615 force CS3 to 0.

With SEL1 = 1, a single-ended conversion of AIN3/REF (MAX11612/MAX11613) or AIN11/REF (MAX11616/MAX11617) is skipped and a scan ends at AIN2 or AIN10. MAX11614/MAX11615 have AIN7 and REF on separate pins, so this does not apply to them.

tables.title: Channel selection in differential mode, SGL/DIF = 0 (Table 4)
notes: MAX11612/MAX11613 force CS3 and CS2 to 0; MAX11614/MAX11615 force CS3 to 0.

With SEL1 = 1, a differential conversion of the AIN2 and AIN3/REF pair (MAX11612/MAX11613) or AIN10 and AIN11/REF pair (MAX11616/MAX11617) treats the REF pin as GND; code 1011, for one, gives GND minus AIN10. MAX11614/MAX11615 are not affected.
A differential scan steps the channel address by 2 until it reaches the limit set by CS3–CS1.

tables.title: Scanning configuration (Table 5)
rows: From AIN0 up to the channel set by CS3–CS0. Codes above 1011 stop at AIN11. With AIN_/REF used as a reference, the scan stops at AIN2 or AIN10.
The channel set by CS3–CS0 is converted eight times.

MAX11612/MAX11613: upper half, from AIN2 up to the channel set by CS1 and CS0; a setting of AIN0, AIN1 or AIN2 converts AIN2 alone; with AIN_/REF as a reference it stops at AIN2. MAX11614/MAX11615: upper quartile, from AIN6 up to the channel set by CS3–CS0; a setting of AIN0–AIN6 converts AIN6 alone. MAX11616/MAX11617: upper half, from AIN6 up to the channel set by CS3–CS0; a setting of AIN0–AIN6 converts AIN6 alone; with AIN_/REF as a reference it stops at the chosen channel or AIN10.
The channel set by CS3–CS0 is converted once.
notes: In external clock mode 01 and 11 behave the same: the part keeps converting until the master answers with a not-acknowledge.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit (MAX11614)
circuits.description: The converter on its own supply rail, talking to a microcontroller over the two-wire bus. VDD has a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground. Eight analog inputs come in on AIN0 to AIN7. An optional 2 kΩ resistor and 0.1 µF capacitor load the REF pin, which is the filter the part needs when its internal reference is driven out on that pin. SDA and SCL each pass through an optional series resistor to the bus, where a pull-up to 5 V holds each line high; the microcontroller runs from that 5 V rail with its own bypass capacitor. On the MAX11612/MAX11613 the network sits on AIN3/REF and on the MAX11616/MAX11617 on AIN11/REF.
notes: U1.2, U1.3 and U1.4 are the three N.C. pins of the 16-pin QSOP.
U2's pins carry the names of the lines and rail they connect to.

circuits.title: Power-supply grounding connection
circuits.description: How the converter's supply and ground meet the rest of the system. The analog rail (3 V or 5 V) reaches VDD through an optional 5 Ω resistor for very noisy supplies; at VDD, 4.7 µF and 0.1 µF in parallel go to the converter's GND. Converter GND and the digital circuitry's ground each run back on their own to the one ground point at the supplies. The digital circuitry has its own 3 V/5 V logic rail.
notes: Only the supply and ground pins of U1 are shown.

operation.text: Six 12-bit SAR converters with an I2C-compatible bus, built-in track/hold, reference and clock. MAX11612/MAX11613 have 4 inputs, MAX11614/MAX11615 have 8 and MAX11616/MAX11617 have 12. The even-numbered parts run from 4.5 V to 5.5 V with a 4.096 V internal reference; the odd-numbered parts run from 2.7 V to 3.6 V with 2.048 V. Any of them takes an external reference from 1 V to VDD. Pin-compatible 10-bit (MAX11606–MAX11611) and 8-bit (MAX11600–MAX11605) versions exist. The process is BiCMOS.

Inputs pass a multiplexer to a fully differential sampling capacitor, then a comparator working against a differential switched-capacitor DAC. Results go to a FIFO memory of one 12-bit word per channel: 4, 8 or 12 words by part.

While tracking, CT/H charges to the selected input; at hold it keeps that charge and the DAC spends 12 clock cycles bringing the comparator input back to zero. Source impedance up to 1.5 kΩ costs little accuracy. Above that, 100 pF from the input to GND helps but narrows the bandwidth; larger sources want a buffer amplifier.

Internal clock: tracking starts on the 8th rising SCL edge of the address byte, hold on the falling edge of the 9th (acknowledge) clock, and the part then holds SCL low while it converts. External clock: tracking starts on the rising edge during the R/W bit, hold begins as the second clock rises during the first result byte, and the conversion takes the next 12 clocks.
The track circuit has 5 MHz small-signal bandwidth, so periodic signals above the sampling rate can be undersampled. An anti-alias filter is advised to keep unwanted high frequencies out of band.
Diodes clamp each analog input to VDD and GND, so the pins survive (GND − 0.3 V) to (VDD + 0.3 V). Conversions stay accurate only while inputs go no more than 50 mV below GND or above VDD.
SGL/DIF = 1 measures the selected input against GND (Table 3); SGL/DIF = 0 measures the selected pair (Table 4). Single-ended conversions are always unipolar, 0 to VREF, whatever BIP/UNI says.
In differential mode BIP/UNI picks the range: unipolar is 0 to VREF in straight binary, and a negative difference reads as code 0; bipolar is ±VREF/2 in two's complement.

SDA and SCL need pull-ups of 750 Ω or more. Optional series resistors RS guard the inputs against bus spikes and reduce crosstalk and undershoot. Data on SDA must not change while SCL is high; a change then is a START (high to low) or STOP (low to high). A repeated START keeps the bus and its speed mode. Each byte is acknowledged on the 9th clock: the receiver pulls SDA low for an acknowledge or leaves it high for a not-acknowledge. Moving data in or out takes at least 18 clocks.

The 7-bit address is fixed at the factory: 0110100 for MAX11612/MAX11613, 0110011 for MAX11614/MAX11615, 0110101 for MAX11616/MAX11617. The address byte's LSB is R/W: 0 writes, 1 reads. The part acknowledges a matching address by pulling SDA low for one clock.

The part starts in fast/standard mode, good for up to 22.2 ksps. Conversion rates up to 94.4 ksps need high-speed mode: the master sends the code 0000 1XXX, the part answers with a not-acknowledge and switches to HS mode, and the master follows with a repeated START and the address. A STOP returns the part to fast/standard mode.

After the address with R/W = 0 the master writes one or two bytes, in either order. A byte with MSB 1 is the setup byte (Table 1); MSB 0 makes it the configuration byte (Table 2). The cycle ends with a STOP or repeated START.

After the address with R/W = 1, each result comes as two bytes: four high bits, then the 12 data bits MSB first. The master acknowledges to keep reading or sends a not-acknowledge to stop, after which the part frees SDA.

CLK = 0, the power-up default. The internal oscillator runs the conversions while the part stretches SCL low, up to 8.3 µs per channel; a scan runs all its conversions before SCL is released. Results then read out first-in first-out at up to 1.7 MHz; reading past the last result wraps to the first. Only results of the current conversion are held, so new data needs a fresh read command. Holding SCL quiet during conversion lowers system noise and frees the master.

CLK = 1: SCL is the conversion clock. Tracking starts on the 9th rising edge of the address byte and the conversion two clocks later; data follow right after the four leading high bits, and conversions continue by scan mode until a not-acknowledge, with no readdressing. A conversion has to finish within 1 ms or droop on the hold capacitor spoils it, so with an SCL period above 60 µs use the internal clock. External clock is required from 40 ksps to 94.4 ksps; below 40 ksps the internal clock draws much less power.

SCAN[1:0] choose the scan (Table 5). Results land in memory in conversion order and read back the same way, two bytes each, every byte acknowledged by the master or the transfer stops. Memory cannot be read without converting. With AIN_/REF set as a reference (SEL1 = 1) that pin drops out of scans; MAX11614/MAX11615 have a separate REF pin and are unaffected.
At power-up: single-ended, unipolar, one conversion of AIN0, internal clock, VDD as reference, and AIN_/REF an analog input. Memory contents are undefined.

Between conversions the analog circuits power down by themselves; the internal reference stays up because it takes long to wake. With an external clock the part goes idle only once the master ends the read (STOP, repeated START or not-acknowledge); with the internal clock it powers down once results are in memory. With an external or VDD reference, shutdown current is under 0.5 µA. Results taken with the internal clock stay in memory through shutdown until a STOP or repeated START. A valid address wakes the part. For the MAX11613 average current is 60 µA at 10 ksps, 6 µA at 1 ksps and 1 µA (3 µW) at 0.1 ksps.

SEL[2:0] set the reference and the AIN_/REF pin (Table 6). With AIN_/REF a reference input or output, a differential conversion that uses it sees GND in its place, and single-ended scans stop at AIN2 or AIN10.

4.096 V on MAX11612/MAX11614/MAX11616, 2.048 V on MAX11613/MAX11615/MAX11617. It needs 10 ms to wake: power it 10 ms before a conversion, or keep it on (SEL0). Once on it stays on until reconfigured; in shutdown its output is high impedance. Brought out on AIN_/REF (SEL[2:1] = 11) it takes 2 kΩ in series and 0.1 µF to GND. It must not supply outside circuits, needs no bypass capacitor, and performs best left unconnected (SEL1 = 0). With an external or VDD reference there is no wake-up delay.
Any voltage from 1 V to VDD. For full accuracy the source must deliver up to 40 µA with an output impedance of 500 kΩ or less; a higher-impedance or noisy source gets 0.1 µF to GND right at AIN_/REF.

Build on a printed board, not wire-wrap. Keep analog and digital traces apart, never parallel, and no digital traces under the package. Separate analog and digital grounds, joined at one star point, with a short low-impedance return to the supply. Decouple VDD to star ground through 0.1 µF in parallel with 4.7 µF, as close to the pin as possible with short leads; a 5 Ω series resistor helps on a very noisy supply.

INL is measured against the endpoint line once offset and gain are removed. DNL is a step's departure from 1 LSB; below 1 LSB guarantees every code appears and the transfer only rises. Aperture jitter is the sample-to-sample spread of the sampling instant; aperture delay is the time from the sampling clock's falling edge to the actual sample. SNR excludes the fundamental, the first five harmonics and DC. SFDR compares the fundamental with the largest other spur.
